{{short description|Catalan mathematician and statistician (1944-2015)}}
'''Evarist Giné-Masdéu''' (July 31, 1944 – March 13, 2015), or simply '''Evarist Giné''', was a Catalan mathematician and statistician. He is known for his pioneering works in probability in [[Banach space|Banach spaces]], [[empirical process theory]], [[U-statistics]] and processes, and [[nonparametric statistics]].<ref name=IMS>{{cite web |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Obituary: Evarist Giné-Masdeu, 1944–2015 |url=https://imstat.org/2015/05/18/obituary-evarist-gine-masdeu-1944-2015/ |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Evarist Giné, Mathematics Department Head, Dies |url=https://today.uconn.edu/2015/03/evarist-gine-mathematics-department-head-dies/ |website=UConn Today |date=17 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Evarist Giné-Masdéu (1944-2015) |url=https://bernoullisociety.org/2013-11-19-07-52-58/15-features/220-evarist-gine-masdeu-1944-2015 |website=bernoullisociety.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Koltchinskii |first1=Vladimir |last2=Nickl |first2=Richard |last3=van de Geer |first3=Sara |last4=Wellner |first4=Jon A. |title=The mathematical work of Evarist Giné |journal=Stochastic Processes and Their Applications |date=December 2016 |volume=126 |issue=12 |pages=3607–3622 |doi=10.1016/j.spa.2016.05.005|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Giné was born in [[Falset, Tarragona|Falset]] in [[Catalonia]]. He studied at the [[University of Barcelona]], obtaining a [[Licentiate (degree)|Licenciatura]] degree in 1967. He went to the United States and completed his PhD at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1973 under the supervision of [[Richard M. Dudley]]. He was a lecturer in statistics at University of California, Berkeley from 1974 to 1975. He spent time afterwards at the [[Venezuelan Institute for Scientific Research]], where he was the head of the mathematics department, before moving back to the United States.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dudley |first=R. M. |date=2016-12-01 |title=Reminiscences, and some explorations about the bootstrap |journal=Stochastic Processes and Their Applications |series=In Memoriam: Evarist Giné |volume=126 |issue=12 |pages=3623–3631 |doi=10.1016/j.spa.2016.04.016 |issn=0304-4149|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 1983, Giné became a professor at [[Texas A&M University]] and later moved to [[College of Staten Island]] of the [[City University of New York]] in 1988.<ref> [https://archives.library.csi.cuny.edu/omeka/files/original/d1e37aab54c6ca86503dc77d57deb101.pdf "Here's the New Faculty"], ''The College Voice'', The College of Staten Island, Staten Island, New York, volume IX, number 3, November 1, 1988, page 12.</ref> He became a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Connecticut]] in 1990, and was the head of the department of mathematics from 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-03-25 |title=Math Department Head Evarist Giné dies at 70 |url=https://dailycampusarchive.wordpress.com/2015/03/25/math-department-head-evarist-gine-dies-at-70/ |access-date=2023-12-28 |website=dailycampusarchive |language=en}}</ref> He stayed at the University of Connecticut until his death.<ref name=IMS></ref>
